ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: in the bird head image labeled “Before” on the left, the beak is smaller; in the bird head image labeled “After” on the right, the beak is obviously larger, and the bracket beside it also shows that the latter beak size has increased. Then reason: this is not a single individual making its beak “grow larger,” but rather heritable variation related to larger beaks in the population being more likely to survive and reproduce under environmental pressure. As time passes, the frequency of this favorable gene/allele rises, so the mechanism that best explains the change in beak size is natural selection, that is, environmental selection pressure causing gene frequency to change.

method.method_draft: First describe the visual change: the image compares a bird before and after, and the beak-size bracket is larger in the after panel. Interpret this as a population trait changing over generations, not one bird stretching its beak. Then connect the trait to heritable genetic variation: birds with genes for the favored beak size survived or reproduced more under environmental conditions, so those gene variants increased in frequency. Conclude that the mechanism is environmental selective pressure causing a change in gene/allele frequency, i.e., natural selection.
